intro: Monotonicity audits identify records that arrive out of expected temporal order. Sorting first would hide the very issue the audit needs to expose.
task: Report every adjacent timestamp decrease without sorting the observations.
requirements: times contains integer timestamps in +/-1e9. Return [index, previous, current] for every adjacent decrease where current < previous. Equal timestamps are allowed; do not sort or compare only against the running maximum.
Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Integer inputs must be Python ints, excluding bool, within the task-specific bounds or -1e9..1e9 when no narrower bounds are stated.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Compare each timestamp with exactly its preceding observation.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Keep original positions so the report points to the observed ordering error.

explanation: Monotonicity audits identify records that arrive out of expected temporal order. Sorting first would hide the very issue the audit needs to expose.
A local decrease differs from being below the historical maximum. After one decrease, later increasing timestamps are valid adjacent transitions even if still below an earlier peak.
